pages.termsLead: Pomysłownik! shows information about existing innovations gathered from public sources. By using the service you agree to the rules below.
pages.terms1: The content of the cards must not be used to infringe the authors' intellectual property: copying solutions, filing patent applications for others' inventions or impersonating owners.
pages.terms2: Cards are a search aid. Before any decision, check the source and contact the owner through their public page.
pages.terms3: Values labelled as estimates are computed from public data and may be imprecise. Confirmed values point to a source.
pages.terms4: Personal data: we store the email, role, organisation and interests given at registration. You can delete them in your profile. Usage statistics are aggregated and hold no identifiers.
pages.terms5: The service is a prototype from the Hacknation 2026 hackathon (PCI task). The code is available under EUPL-1.2.
pages.accessibilityLead: We want Pomysłownik! to be usable by everyone. Here we say what we checked, what we have not checked yet and which limitations we know of. Status on 22.11.2026.
pages.a11yStatus1: We follow WCAG 2.2 at level AA.
pages.a11yStatus2: The service partly conforms to this standard. The automated test and the keyboard walk found no serious problems, but some checks are still to come, and we describe a few limitations below.
pages.a11yFeaturesTitle: What makes it easier to use
pages.a11yFeature1: In the account menu you can set the text size (100, 125 or 150%) and the contrast (standard, high or low). We remember your choice on this device.
pages.a11yFeature2: We respect your system settings: reduced motion (only short fades remain), preferred contrast and forced colours.
pages.a11yFeature3: Everything works with the keyboard, and the focused element always has a visible outline. The first link on every page is “Skip to content”. The Esc key closes the card, menus and the filter panel.
pages.a11yFeature4: The interface is in Polish, English and Ukrainian. The language of the page and of quotations is marked, so screen readers use the right pronunciation. The exception is described under known limitations.
pages.a11yFeature5: Colour is never the only signal: every status has an icon and a word. Scores are numbers, and every number has a source.
pages.a11yChecked1: An automated axe-core 4.14 test (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules at levels A and AA, plus best practices) on 13 views: sign-in, registration, search, results, results with filters, the phone filter panel, a card with all parts opened, a missing card, sources, profile and the three information pages. Each view in 14 settings: 1440, 390 and 320 px wide, 200% zoom with 150% text, three languages, high and low contrast, forced colours. 176 runs in total.
pages.a11yChecked2: Result: no critical or moderate errors. We checked two kinds of serious reports by hand. In forced colours mode the tool reports low contrast on 12 views, but the browser shows system colours with full contrast there, so this is an error of the tool. At 320 px wide one checkbox in the filter panel is covered by a fraction of a pixel by the button at the bottom of the panel; after scrolling it is fully available. Two minor technical notes about element roles remain (the phone filter panel and the settings in the account menu).
pages.a11yChecked3: A walk with the Tab key through each of these views at 1440 and 390 px, in high contrast and in forced colours (49 walks). Every focused element has a visible outline, and focus never lands on hidden or covered elements.
pages.a11yChecked4: Horizontal scrolling at 320 px wide (also with 150% text) and at 200% zoom with 150% text. At 200% zoom the account menu and the example cards went past the edge of the screen. We fixed that. We also fixed the logo, which could not be seen in forced colours, and made checkboxes 24 px.
pages.a11yChecked5: Colour contrast measured with the WCAG 2.2 formula: every pair of text and background meets level AA (at least 4.5:1). Before this, three manual accessibility reviews of the code and screenshots took place. Their fixes are live.
pages.a11yNotCheckedTitle: What we have not checked yet
pages.a11yNotChecked1: Use with a screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA). This test is planned.
pages.a11yNotChecked2: Real phones and tablets. We checked the phone view in a browser that simulates it.
pages.a11yNotChecked3: The Safari and Firefox browsers. We ran all tests in Chrome.
pages.a11yLimit1: If a card's text does not exist in the language you chose, we show it in another language. Such text is not yet marked with its language, so a screen reader may read it with the wrong pronunciation. We will fix this once the server sends the language of each text.
pages.a11yLimit2: The Ukrainian interface is a machine translation. It is waiting to be checked by a person who knows the language.
pages.a11yLimit3: Technical values (numbers, identifiers, addresses) use a fixed-width typeface. In the Ukrainian version some of them may show in a different typeface from the rest of the text.
pages.a11yReport: If something makes the service hard to use, <link>write to us</link>. Tell us the page and describe what happened. The same contact is in the account menu under “Help and contact”.
pages.methodologyLead: How an innovation card is made and what its numbers mean.
pages.m1Text: Public sources: RAD-on, OpenAlex, university and institution websites, the Technology Transfer Platform, PDF reports. Through APIs, web crawling and document analysis. Every source has a retrieval date and a quote.
pages.m2Text: A value confirmed by a source is labelled “Confirmed” with a link to the source. A computed value is labelled “Estimate” with its method. The language model never produces numbers: scores are computed by code from stored evidence.
pages.m3Text: Implementation level (concept, prototype, testing, pilot, in practice). TRL 1–9 for technology only. Innovativeness: similarity to other cards and works. Application potential: transferability to other organisations. Credibility: the number and quality of sources and confirmations.
pages.m4Text: Oslo Manual (2018): a new or improved solution, significantly different from earlier ones, available or in use. Every card shows the result of this test for the three conditions.
pages.m5Text: The database is a prototype. Sources may be out of date (the card then carries “Out of date”). We collect no data about private individuals and do not mediate contact.

hero.t1: Polish innovations from public sources, in one place.
hero.l1: Technological, educational and administrative. Every number comes with its source and date.
hero.t2: A fact is a fact, an estimate is an estimate.
hero.l2: Implementation level, TRL and three scores. You always see what a source confirms and what the model computed.
hero.t3: For public offices, universities, schools, companies and inventors.
hero.l3: A view that fits what you are looking for: a deployment, a partner or an idea.
hero.t4: Sign in, type a topic, open a card.
hero.l4: No forms and no training. You see the first card after three clicks.
